tools.name: search_specs
tools.description: Finds specs on Spekkr by words, the best match first, with each one's id, summary and platforms. Most build a part of an app; a spec that builds something else, such as a CAD model, a circuit or an animation, says so under kind. Search with a few words that name the thing, such as "sign in" or "slid

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Returns everything Spekkr knows about one spec: its manifest (what it builds, what the person may change under customize, the files, what it needs, the commands and secrets it uses under safety, the changelog). Read it before pull_spec to learn which choices the spec offers. versions says which vers

tools.name: pull_spec
tools.description: Returns a spec's files, ready to write into a folder and build from: BUILD.md (how to build), spekkr.json (the manifest), spekkr.inputs.json (the person's choices) and the spec files. It checks the choices first and refuses a key the spec does not declare or a value it does not offer. Anything not c

tools.name: get_spec_file
tools.description: Returns one file of a spec as text. Use it for a file pull_spec listed without content, unless its note says to download it. A long file comes in parts: when the answer has nextLine, call again with that line. Give version to read the file as a kept earlier version has it.

tools.name: get_spec_changes
tools.description: Says what changed in a spec between two versions, so a build of an earlier version can be brought up to date without starting over. tools.name: get_feedback
tools.description: Returns what Spekkr members reported about a spec, the newest first. tools.name: check_spec
tools.description: Checks a spec someone is writing against Spekkr's listing rules and returns every problem at once. Pass the text of its spekkr.json. Pass its text files too, as files, and the answer adds advice: things in the text worth a look, such as a requirement with no Accept when line or a choice no file ment

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Says which Spekkr account the caller is signed in as, which specs it has published, and how each one is doing: under numbers, its newest version, its pulls, its stars, and where there are any its followers and feedback. Only the account itself is told these numbers. This tool needs sign-in: the firs

tools.name: fork_spec
tools.description: Starts a fork of a spec a member published: a spec of the signed-in person's own that begins as a copy and names the first one under lineage.forkedFrom. It returns the fork's spekkr.json, its files and keepFrom, ready to give to publish_spec, and the source's license when it states one. Nothing is p

tools.name: publish_spec
tools.description: Publishes a spec on Spekkr under the signed-in person's username, as username/name, or publishes a new version of one of theirs. tools.name: unpublish_spec
tools.description: Takes one of the signed-in person's specs off Spekkr: its page, its files, every earlier version Spekkr keeps, and its place in search. To take down one earlier version only, use unpublish_spec_version. The versions it had stay used up, so publishing it again needs a higher version. This tool needs

tools.name: unpublish_spec_version
tools.description: Takes one earlier version of one of the signed-in person's specs off Spekkr: its page and its files. The spec stays listed, and its other versions stay as they are. The version's number stays used. The newest version cannot be taken off this way: unpublish_spec takes the whole spec down. This tool n

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tells a spec's publisher, and everyone who reads its page, how a build went. kind is worked (the build did what the spec says), problem (something in the spec was wrong, missing or unclear) or idea (a request or a suggestion). Give the version that was built, as spekkr.inputs.json has it, and the re

tools.name: answer_feedback
tools.description: Answers one entry of the feedback on a spec the signed-in person published, closes it, or opens it again. answer is plain text of up to 1,000 characters, shown under the entry with the publisher's username; a new answer takes the place of the one before. close true closes the entry. closedIn names t

tools.name: remove_feedback
tools.description: Takes one entry off a spec's feedback for good. The person who sent an entry can take their own back, and Spekkr's operators can remove any entry. A spec's publisher cannot remove feedback on their spec: answer_feedback answers it. This tool needs sign-in. Ask the person before you call it.

tools.name: follow_spec
tools.description: Follows a spec for the signed-in person, or stops following it. Give the spec's id, and on as false to stop.
